business_impact: Customers can create tickets but ticket-detail reads return HTTP 504 while the downstream policy service exceeds the API timeout budget.
reproduction: Deploy the APP-002 exercise release, attach the controlled downstream service with approximately three-second response latency, create a valid customer ticket, then GET /api/tickets/<id>. The API returns HTTP 504 while readiness and core dependency health remain HTTP 200. A direct probe with a larger timeout returns HTTP 200 from the downstream service after approximately three seconds.
evidence: failing request ID retained from the Nginx response
same request ID appears in Nginx and API logs
API log contains dependency_timeout for app002-policy-service
Tempo and Loki contain the failing request correlation
PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Nginx, and readiness remain healthy
direct downstream probe returns HTTP 200 but exceeds the one-second application timeout budget
same API release succeeds when dependency latency normalizes
full customer/release verification passes after dependency recovery
steps_already_performed: confirmed customer scope and affected route
checked PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Nginx and readiness
measured downstream reachability and response latency directly
correlated public request through Nginx, API, Loki and Tempo
re-tested original symptom and complete customer journey after dependency recovery
requested_action: Dependency/service owner to investigate the latency excursion and provide preventive controls. Application owner should review whether the one-second timeout, retry policy, fallback behavior, and user-facing 504 handling remain appropriate, but no application code fault is claimed by this incident evidence.
